$doc: The negative-test matrix for scripts/check-boundaries.mjs, as data.
Every case is a whole miniature repo: `base` below, plus this case's `files`,
minus its `remove`. The checker is then run against it as a child process, at
arm's length, exactly as CI runs it — no import of its internals, so the thing
under test is the shipped gate rather than a copy of its regexes.
WHY THIS IS JSON AND NOT A .mjs MODULE. The sources below contain deliberate
boundary violations. check-boundaries.mjs scans every .mjs/.js/.cjs/.ts file in
the repo and cannot tell a string containing `import "../lib/x.js"` from an
import — so holding these cases in a JavaScript file would fail the very gate
they exist to test. A .json file is not scanned. That is also the honest
shape: this is a table, and it reads as one.
`expect.exit` 1 means the case must FAIL the gate; `expect.exit` 0 means it
must PASS. The passing cases are not filler — a rule that bans css/ or
design-system/ from js/, or that reads a path out of a comment, breaks the
pages and the css gate, and nothing else in the repo would notice.

cases.name: the clean fixture passes
cases.form: control — the baseline every failure below is attributable to

cases.name: static import across a slice: js/ imports lib/knowledge
dynamic import across a slice: api/ imports evals/
cases.form: dynamic import() — invisible to the old regex, which required a quote after `import`

cases.name: path read across a slice: evals/ reads api/ through new URL
cases.form: readFileSync(new URL(…)) — invisible to the old regex, and the idiom the architecture itself runs on

cases.name: path read across a slice: lib/knowledge reads content/ source
cases.form: fs read of a bare string path

cases.name: design-system internals, reached dynamically from js/
js/ may POST to /api/chat
cases.form: control — fetch is an HTTP call, not a dependency

cases.name: js/ may read the published corpus and the published stylesheets
cases.form: control — banning css/ or design-system/ here would break both pages and scripts/check-css.mjs

cases.name: lib/knowledge may read content/dist/content.json by path
cases.form: control — the crossing the whole architecture is built on

cases.name: a banned path quoted in a comment is documentation, not a dependency
cases.form: control — false positives are how a gate loses its readers

cases.name: a bare package specifier is a dependency, not a slice
cases.form: control — `import { z } from "zod"` must not read as a path
